Edge-Preserving Splatting with Compression/Stretching is a volume rendering technique that sharpens discontinuities in low-resolution or undersampled data by applying non-linear transformations to the standard splatting kernel footprint [S1].

The claim states that Edge-Preserving Splatting with Compression/Stretching is a volume rendering technique that sharpens discontinuities in low-resolution or undersampled data by applying non-linear transformations to the standard splatting kernel footprint. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this: it describes the method as applying 'non-linear compression and stretching functions to the standard splatting kernel' to 'preserve sharp edges' (sharpens discontinuities). It notes that the method produces 'much sharper decreasing regions and nice sharp edges, especially visible in low-resolution or undersampled data.' The text further details the use of 'stretching/compressing function map(x)' to modify the footprint and mentions that small structures in undersampled data are often challenging, which this method addresses.
supported
